newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik government says repelled new rebel assault.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government says repelled new rebel assault.

text.p: Tajikistan's defence ministry said on Thursday its forces had fended off an attack by Islamist rebels east of the capital Dushanbe.
But government military sources said fighting still raged in the same area, some 300 km (200 miles) from the capital.
"Early on November 21, armed oppsition forces carried out an attack on a government military post at the Khaburabad Pass," the defence ministry said in a statement.
"The attack was repulsed," it said, adding that several of its troops had been wounded, two of them badly.

The military sources said there was still fighting around the pass, which straddles the only road between government territory in the west of the impoverished former Soviet republic and its mountainous eastern half, which is largely controlled by the armed Islamic opposition.
The four-year civil war has cost tens of thousands of lives while refugees have fled to neighbouring Afghanistan.
Earlier this month, U.N. military observers said they were "gravely concerned" by a recent flare-up in fighting which flouts a U.N.-sponsored ceasefire reconfirmed last July.
